page.layout: One column of running text, set in the centre of the page. No marginal notes, no page number, no running head. Below the last line, at the right, the word "minister-" is printed as a catchword.

main_text.p: 1. In genere : Etenim hæ distinctiones impingunt in omnes bonæ distributionis regulas: & perinde se habent, ac si quis distingueret Unum, in unum & unum, id est, non unum sed multa : Caput in caput & caput, id est, capita ; imò Ens, in ens & non ens. Ex S.Scriptura namque evicimus, Petram illam, supra quam ędificatur[?] Ecclesia,esse Individuum & Singulare: ideoque non posse aliis numero distinctis attribui: hoc enim speciērum est : Quemadmodum Sol, quia unus est, non potest distingui in Principalem & ministerialem, visibilem & invisibilem, &c. ita Beatæ Virginis Filius unus est, ideoque hoc nomen, sub nulla distinctione, pluribus tribui potest.

Nullâ quoque legitimâ distinctione unum Correlatum, in se & correlatum distingui potest: ex. gr. Rex singularis, in Regem & Subditum : neq; correlatum aut correlati membrum singulare, nomen recipit correlati: ex. gr. Membrum corporis aut totū corpus,non potest dici Caput: minimè Sponsa appellari Sponsus:
main_text.l: Christus est caput, Petrus est membrum:
Itaq; nomen Christi Petro tribui nequit:
main_text.p: Ratio : quia Caput hoc, Sponsus hic, Dominus iste, non est species, sed individuum & relatum singulare.
Omne autem distributum, Species sive univoca sive analoga esse debet.

Denique cum Petra hæc non minus sit singularissima atq; Deus seu Dei essentia. 1.Tim.2.5.[?] & præter hanc nulla alia esse possit ; sicut nec præter Deum alius est, necesse est alterum distributionis hujus membrum esse non ens: non minus enim Petra hæc distingui potest in Petram principalem & minister-

page.notes: Readings with [?]: "ędificatur" (the letter under the e-cedilla mark is uncertain) and the final "5" in the citation "1.Tim.2.5." (printed with a doubtful numeral). "speciērum" is printed "speciērum" with a macron-like mark over the e; kept as read. The word "minister-" at the foot is treated as a catchword because it stands alone at the right below the last line; it is also the start of the next page's word. Faint show-through from the reverse side is ignored.
